ui_bugs.issue: CRITICAL REGRESSION: Landing on /dashboard (or any protected route) with a valid session cookie still redirects to /onboarding on first load. Iteration 1's fix (adding setLoading(true) inside refresh()) is present but insufficient because refresh() only runs from useEffect AFTER render — so on the render where AuthContext.user just transitioned null→truthy, BusinessProvider still has {loading:false, business:null} from the previous !user branch, and AppShell fires <Navigate to='/onboarding'> before the next refresh() effect runs. Reproduced 2x in this iteration. Workaround still works: land on /onboarding, wait ~3s, then client-side navigate to /dashboard.

action_items: FIX-1 (CRITICAL, repeat): Properly close the BusinessContext loading race. The current setLoading(true) inside refresh() runs too late (inside useEffect after render). Options: (a) In BusinessProvider, add `useEffect(() => { if (user) setLoading(true); }, [user]);` BEFORE the refresh effect so user->truthy transition synchronously queues loading=true for the very next render; OR (b) derive `loading` state: `const effectiveLoading = authLoading || loading || (user && business === null && !businessErrored);`; OR (c) in AppShell, also gate redirect on AuthContext.loading and don't redirect while user just became truthy and business fetch hasn't started yet. Recommend (b) — most robust. Verify by hitting /dashboard directly with test_session_screenshot_tok cookie — must NOT bounce to /onboarding.

rca of the issue.onboarding_redirect_race_still_present: AuthContext transitions user from null→object asynchronously after /api/auth/me resolves. When user is null, BusinessProvider.refresh's first branch runs setBusiness(null)+setLoading(false). When user becomes truthy, React re-renders BusinessProvider AND its children (including AppShell) with the new user but still-stale {business:null, loading:false}. AppShell's redirect condition (user && !loading && !business) is now true → <Navigate to='/onboarding'>. THEN the useEffect for refresh() fires and calls setLoading(true), but the route change has already unmounted AppShell so it doesn't matter. The setLoading(true) added inside refresh() cannot fix this because refresh() runs from useEffect which is post-render — the bad render window opens BEFORE any effect runs. Correct fix: make loading derived (loading || (user && business === null)) OR add a synchronous-effect that flips loading true on user change BEFORE the render children see the new user (impossible with useEffect; requires state-in-render pattern or derived state).
